title: sdks: auth/retries + streaming parity fixes across python/typescript/go, bump v1.72.0
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: This PR consolidates a set of SDK parity fixes and ergonomics improvements across Python, TypeScript, and Go focused on auth behavior, retry/unary-streaming parity, and streaming ergonomics required for v1.72.0. Motivation: customers reported subtle differences between SDKs when using streaming endpoints (inconsistent retry semantics on auth failures, different backpressure/flush behavior, and missing convenience overloads). Goals: 1) unify auth retry middleware so transient 401/429 responses trigger consistent backoff and token refresh across all SDKs; 2) align streaming API ergonomics so start/stop/cleanup and error propagation match server expectations; 3) fix parity gaps (parameter names, default timeouts, telemetry headers) and bump SDK versions to v1.72.0. What changed: - Python SDK: refactor AuthTransport to centralize token refresh and retryable-status handling; add streaming iterator helper with proper cancellation semantics; expose retry config via ClientConfig.retry_policy; update CI matrix to include 3.11/3.12/3.13. - TypeScript SDK: introduce AuthInterceptor with unified refresh + retry; refactor streaming ReadableStream wrapper to forward end/error events and provide an asyncIterator convenience; add types for RetryPolicy and default sensible timeouts; update bundling config. - Go SDK: add auth middleware to http.Client wrapper with refresh-on-401 and backoff; implement StreamReader with context-aware cancellation; export RetryPolicy struct and default constants. - Tests: add cross-language integration tests (local mock server) for auth-retry on streaming endpoints and flaky network simulation; unit tests for new helpers. - Docs: SDK CHANGELOG entries and a short migration guide for teams relying on previous retry behavior. Compatibility notes: changes are backwards-compatible for the vast majority of callers; default retry/backoff parameters are conservative but configurable. There is a minor surface change: streaming helper names were added (not removed) so migration is optional. QA and rollout: CI passed including cross-SDK e2e, staged rollout to internal customers for one week before public release; monitoring hooks added to Redwood Console for early regression detection. Related: closes ENG-4523, addresses SUP-2331.
